title: Why 30‑Year Bonds Aren’t a Safe ‘Set‑and‑Forget’ Bet

scenes.text: Is a 30‑year Treasury at 6% really a risk‑free retirement plan?
scenes.query2: long term bond risk free myth

scenes.text: Historically, 30‑year US Treasury yields average about 4.5% over the past 30 years, not the current 6% spike.
At 6% inflation, a bond’s real return turns negative – you lose purchasing power each year.
Don’t rely on a single bond – diversify with stocks and inflation‑protected assets.
scenes.label: DIVERSIFY
scenes.sub: Mix bonds, stocks, TIPS for real growth

scenes.text: Follow if you're done staying broke.

description: A 6% yield looks tempting, but inflation can erase those gains. Discover why diversification beats the “set‑and‑forget” bond myth.
